Subject: Follow-up: Security & Compliance discovery - FinCo

Hi Sarah -

Thanks again for taking the call this morning - good conversation and really helpful context on FinCo's security bar. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Key takeaways from today
- Compliance needs: SOC 2 Type II report required for procurement; GDPR controls for EU user data; potential HIPAA considerations for tokenized PII in a later phase.
- Scope ask: FinCo wants vendor scope to cover inference endpoints and embedding storage (logs/kv cache) - explicitly called out.
- Questions you raised: encryption at rest + KMS/HSM options, data residency, and audit log availability.

Attachments: I'm attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire for you to fill out (vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx). If you prefer, we can open this in OneTrust or send via DocuSign - whatever works for procurement.

Proposed next steps
1) You: Share completed questionnaire or indicate which format you prefer by EOD Wed (2026-11-18).
2) Us: I'll attach a SOC 2 summary (we'll send the full report after an NDA/procurement step) + answer your encryption/KMS questions.
3) Schedule a follow-up call with your security team (Rishi/our security) - propose Thurs 11/19 at 10am PT.

MAP (mutual action plan) items
- Vendor questionnaire returned (owner: FinCo procurement) - target 11/18
- SOC 2 evidence request & redlines (owner: Redwood/security) - deliver within 2 business days after questionnaire
- Security review call scheduled (owner: both) - target 11/19

If that looks good I'll proceed to share the SOC 2 stub and answers to the KMS question. Thanks - looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks for the clear recap. That all tracks. A few quick clarifications: 
- Procurement will need a SOC 2 Type II report (prefer PDF) and an attestation letter if possible. Can you share a redacted report?
- For KMS: our default is cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys. We need confirmation that Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) and FIPS-validated HSMs.
- Data residency: we'll need EU region for EU customers; please confirm availability and any additional cost.

We'll aim to get the vendor questionnaire back by 11/18. I've looped in Tom from procurement - he'll handle the questionnaire and initial legal redlines.

Head of Vendor Risk | FinCo

Sarah -

Appreciate the quick reply. Attached is a redacted SOC 2 summary and the stub report (SOC2-report-stub.pdf). We can provide the full report once procurement completes the standard NDA and mutual non-disclosure steps - happy to coordinate with Tom on that flow.

Quick answers to your questions: 
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via integrations with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and can be configured to use HSM-backed keys. We also support bringing your own key material in Dedicated/Private deployments. I'll ask Rishi to confirm FIPS notes for the specific HSM models we commonly integrate with.
- Data residency: EU region is available in our Private and Dedicated offerings; hosted API can route to EU regions on request (we can include in the contract). There may be an additional cost for Dedicated/Private depending on sizing.

I'll add a short tech appendix for the call tomorrow, and we'll be ready to walk through the questionnaire.

Attached: SOC2-report-stub.pdf

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinCo - questionnaire + roadmap ask (prep for 11/19 call)

Rishi / Lauren -

Fwd'ing the thread with FinCo (Sarah/Tom). They're a mid-sized fintech evaluating Redwood for transaction enrichment/embeddings. Quick summary and asks for security prep before the call on 11/19: 

What FinCo needs
- Completed vendor security questionnaire (they'll return by 11/18) - I've attached our questionnaire copy and the SOC2 stub we sent.
- Confirmation of BYOK and HSM/FIPS support (they use HSM-backed keys).
- Scope: include inference endpoints + embedding storage (logs/kv cache) in SOC scope.
- Longer-term: they asked about ISO 27001 roadmap and potential FedRAMP (they're exploring a public sector product in 18-24 months).

Can you please: 
1) Rishi - take the lead on technical answers, confirm FIPS/HSM support and whether any extra documentation is needed for our most common HSM partners (Thales/Luna/AWS CloudHSM). Also advise whether we can commit to including embedding storage in SOC scope and estimated incremental effort.
2) Lauren - can you flag any typical procurement/legal redlines we should expect for fintech customers (especially around data residency and audit logs)?

Timing: Need Rishi's technical notes by EOB 11/17 so I can incorporate into the call deck. Also any ask on estimated timeline/cost for ISO 27001 readiness and FedRAMP feasibility (high level is fine).

Thanks - will keep the call invite pending 11/19 10am PT.

Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: FinCo - questionnaire + roadmap ask (prep for 11/19 call)

Marissa / Lauren -

Quick notes ahead of tomorrow's call: 

KMS/HSM
- Confirmed: we support BYOK for AWS KMS & Google KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed key stores (AWS CloudHSM / Luna). FIPS 140-2/140-3 boundaries depend on the HSM provider - we'll provide vendor-specific statements.

SOC scope expansion (embedding storage + inference endpoints)
- Feasibility: yes, we can include embedding storage (KV cache and persisted embeddings) in SOC scope but this requires: 
  - documentation updates (control mapping),
  - additional evidence collection around retention and access controls, and
  - one extra audit cycle to validate those controls (adds ~2-3 months to timeline if we start now).

ISO 27001 / FedRAMP roadmap (high-level)
- ISO 27001: achievable in ~9-12 months with focused effort (policy gaps, risk assessment, evidence collection). Costs vary by scope and whether we leverage an external consultant.
- FedRAMP: multi-year effort and significant controls mapping; feasible if customer mandates it for public sector use but would require Dedicated/Private deployment architecture and long lead times (12-24+ months).

Vendor questionnaire / evidence
- I'll take the questionnaire and pre-fill technical sections; will flag any items that will need SOC evidence. I recommend we upload evidence to the shared security drive and provide a short evidence index for FinCo.

Next immediate steps (for tomorrow)
- I'll draft technical answers and the FIPS/HSM vendor notes by EOB today (uploaded to drive link).
- Marissa: if procurement requests the full report, we should route via NDA/DocuSign.

Rishi
Director, Applied Security | Redwood Inference
